rates.explainer: Treasury yields are the interest rate the US government pays to borrow. The 2-year follows what traders expect the Fed to do with rates; the 10-year reflects longer-run growth and inflation. Rising yields usually weigh on Nasdaq stocks, because the future profits that tech prices depend on are worth less today when safe bonds pay more. Falling yields usually help.

draft.headline: Nasdaq futures slip 0.88% as an early-week rally fades after Tesla
draft.summary: NQ finished the week down 0.88%. Gains on Monday and Tuesday gave way to three down days, led by Thursday's 1.52% drop. Yields fell over the week, but that did not stop tech from losing ground.
draft.what_it_means: Tesla looked like the week's key moment. It beat on earnings and sales, but its car revenue shrank. NQ's drop grew from −0.16% in the first 21 minutes to −3.01% by the close, but that window overlaps Thursday's slide, so not all of it belongs to Tesla. Thursday's jobless claims were lower than expected, a sign of a firm job market, yet markets barely moved at first. Why NQ fell later is unclear. Tuesday's jump had no clear trigger: ADP had no forecast and the housing figures were missing.
draft.market_reaction: Monday (+1.15%) and Tuesday (+0.69%) were the up days. Then came Wednesday (−0.98%), Thursday (−1.52%, the biggest move) and Friday (−0.20%). S&P 500 futures lost 0.55% for the week, less than tech-heavy NQ. Crude oil rose 2.03% for the week, including +4.14% today, to $103.59. Gold fell 4.21%. The VIX fear gauge slipped 1.00% to 19.45. The dollar was flat at +0.01%.
draft.rates_read: Over the week the 2-year yield fell 3.1bp (1bp is 0.01%) and the 10-year fell 8.4bp. Falling yields usually help Nasdaq stocks, but NQ still fell, so the pressure came from somewhere else. Friday pushed back: the 2-year rose 5.1bp to 4.686% and the 10-year rose 4.8bp to 5.001%. A 10-year yield above 5% is a heavy weight on the value of future tech profits.

draft.learn: A 'beat' is not automatically good news. Tesla beat on earnings and sales, yet NQ fell afterward. Traders also weigh the details, like shrinking car revenue. First reactions can mislead too: NQ's early dip was small, then grew. Always check whether a move holds.
